Overview
This assessment was conducted as part of the WHO South-East (SE) Asia regional initiative to strengthen communicable disease surveillance and strategic information systems. The overarching goal is to inform the development of a regional framework that supports integrated, indicator based surveillance and effective public health response across Member States.
For the Maldives, the assessment aimed to systematically review and map the country’s communicable disease surveillance systems, focusing on their structure, performance, and alignment with international standards. The evaluation covered surveillance for a range of high priority diseases – including tuberculosis (TB), HIV/AIDS, hepatitis B and C, syphilis, gonorrhoea, dengue, chikungunya, leprosy, lymphatic filariasis, malaria, cholera, enteric fever, leptospirosis and
scrub typhus – as well as the broader legal, policy, and operational environment in which these systems function.
The purpose was not only to document the current landscape and identify key gaps, but also to generate actionable recommendations that will help the Maldives and the Region move towards more harmonized, resilient and responsive surveillance – ultimately supporting disease elimination and improved health security.
